evidence: src/domain/task-status.ts: the TASK_STATUSES const, the TaskStatus type and the isTaskStatus guard are the only definition of valid statuses.
src/domain/task.ts: `private status: TaskStatus = "todo"` and markDone() reuse the shared TaskStatus type and throw TaskAlreadyDoneError, so the done-twice rule lives in one place.
src/domain/task-repository.ts: TaskFilter.status is typed as TaskStatus, imported from task-status.ts, so the status set is not duplicated.
src/domain/errors.ts: TaskAlreadyDoneError extends DomainError, giving the module one error hierarchy.

src/domain/project-repository.ts and src/domain/user-repository.ts: both follow the same save/findById port shape and use the Project and User entities from src/domain/project.ts and src/domain/user.ts.
src/domain/id-generator.ts: IdGenerator is a domain port for creating identities, and the application use cases inject it through their constructors.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The src/domain module covers one concern: the task-management domain model. It has the entities (Project, User, Task), the value type for task status (TaskStatus with TASK_STATUSES and isTaskStatus), the domain errors (DomainError, TaskAlreadyDoneError) and the persistence and id-generation ports (ProjectRepository, TaskRepository, UserRepository, IdGenerator). The files use the module's abstractions consistently. Task.ts and task-repository.ts both import TaskStatus from task-status.ts instead of redefining the status literals. Task.markDone throws TaskAlreadyDoneError from errors.ts rather than a bare Error. Each repository refers to its own entity class. Each rule lives in one place: the list of allowed statuses is only in TASK_STATUSES, and the rule that a done task can't be completed again is only in Task.markDone. No file covers an unrelated concern, and no file works around the module's own types.
